examples.en: I put one sugar cube into my coffee.
A sugar cube dissolves quickly in hot water.
The café gave me sugar cubes separately.
Two sugar cubes are sweet enough.
I tried feeding a sugar cube to a horse.
Sugar cubes are square, so they are easy to use.

explain: 네모나게 굳힌 설탕 덩어리예요. 커피나 차에 넣을 때 많이 쓰고, 한 개 두 개로 세요. 가루인 '설탕'보다 양을 맞추기 쉬워요.

phrases.example: 차에 각설탕 한 개만 넣어 주세요.
phrases.en: Please put just one sugar cube in my tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 각설탕은 '한 개, 두 개'처럼 세어서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sugar cubes are counted one by one, like 한 개, 두 개.

phrases.en: I dissolved the sugar cube in warm water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음료에 설탕을 넣고 녹이는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes putting sugar into a drink and letting it dissolve.

phrases.en: I bought a box of sugar cubes at the supermarket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상자에 담아 파는 물건이라 '한 상자'로도 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Since they are sold in boxes, you can also count them as 한 상자.

explain_en: It is sugar pressed into small squares. It is commonly used in coffee or tea and counted as one, two and so on. It is easier to measure than granulated '설탕'.

examples.ko: 저기요, 짜장면 한 그릇은 곱빼기로 주세요.
examples.en: Excuse me, please make one of the jajangmyeon a double portion.

examples.ko: 곱빼기는 이천 원 더 내야 해요.
examples.en: You have to pay 2,000 won more for the double portion.
I was hungry today, so I ordered the double portion.
Which is better, the regular or the double portion?
How much more expensive is the double portion than the regular?

examples.ko: 곱빼기도 혼자 다 먹을 수 있어요!
examples.en: I can finish even the double portion by myself!

explain: 짜장면, 짬뽕, 국밥 같은 식당 메뉴에서 '보통'과 대비해 양을 많이 달라고 할 때 써요. 맞춤법은 '곱배기'가 아니라 '곱빼기'예요.

phrases.en: I was hungry, so I ordered a double portion of jjajangmyeon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 주문할 때 양을 보통보다 훨씬 많이, 두 배 정도로 달라고 한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when ordering food to get a much bigger portion, about double the regular one.

phrases.example: 저는 짬뽕 곱빼기 한 그릇 주세요.
phrases.en: I'd like one double-portion bowl of jjamppong, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 메뉴 이름 뒤에 붙여서 양을 많이 달라고 할 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put it after the menu name to ask for a bigger portion.

phrases.en: Excuse me, please make the gukbap a double portion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 주문할 때 정중하게 양을 많이 달라고 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask for a bigger portion when ordering at a restaurant.

explain_en: At restaurants, you ask for it on dishes like jajangmyeon, jjamppong and gukbap, in contrast to '보통' (regular). The correct spelling is '곱빼기', not '곱배기'.

examples.ko: 쿠키를 만들 때 베이킹파우더를 한 숟갈 넣어요.
examples.en: When I make cookies, I add a spoonful of baking powder.

examples.ko: 베이킹파우더가 없으면 빵이 잘 부풀지 않아요.
examples.en: Without baking powder, the bread doesn't rise well.
I bought baking powder and flour at the supermarket.
I store baking powder in a place without moisture.

examples.ko: 팬케이크 반죽에 베이킹파우더를 너무 많이 넣지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't put too much baking powder in the pancake batter.
Baking powder and baking soda are different from each other.

explain: 빵이나 케이크 반죽을 부풀리는 가루예요. '베이킹소다'와 이름이 비슷하지만 다른 재료라서 레시피에서 바꿔 쓰면 안 돼요. 요리 레시피에서는 '베이킹파우더 1작은술'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Add baking powder to the dough and mix well.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation in recipes.

phrases.en: You need one teaspoon of baking powder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양을 말할 때는 숫자와 단위를 바로 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: State the amount by putting the number and unit right after it.

phrases.en: This pancake has baking powder in it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식에 어떤 재료가 포함되어 있는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say which ingredient a dish contains.

explain_en: It is the powder that makes bread and cake batter rise. The name is similar to '베이킹소다' (baking soda), but they are different ingredients and should not be swapped in a recipe. Recipes write it like '베이킹파우더 1작은술' (1 teaspoon).

examples.ko: 이 멸치볶음은 짭조름해서 밥이랑 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: This stir-fried anchovy is nicely salty, so it goes well with rice.
I keep thinking about the lightly salty french fries.
The soup turned out a little salty.
The sea breeze had a salty smell.

examples.ko: 짭조름한 과자를 먹었더니 물이 마시고 싶어요.
examples.en: I ate a salty snack, so now I want water.
After adding soy sauce, the taste became pleasantly salty.

explain: '짜다'가 소금이 너무 많아 부담스러운 느낌일 때가 많다면, 이 말은 입맛을 당기는 알맞게 짠 맛에 더 어울려요. 밥반찬, 과자, 바닷바람의 냄새에도 써요.

phrases.en: The slightly salty taste suits me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기분 좋게 알맞은 짠맛을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a pleasantly salty taste that is just right.

phrases.en: The soup isn't too salty, just nicely salty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 먹고 바로 말하는 해요체예요. '짜요'보다 부드럽고 좋은 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite-style phrase for saying right after eating. It sounds softer and more positive than '짜요'.

phrases.en: It smells like the salty sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닷바람이나 바다 냄새처럼 소금기가 느껴질 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used when you sense salt, as in sea breeze or the smell of the sea.

explain_en: While '짜다' often feels too salty, this word suits a pleasantly salty taste that makes you want more. It is used for side dishes, snacks and even the smell of the sea breeze.

examples.en: In winter I think of the steamed buns sold on the street.

examples.ko: 찐빵 안에 팥이 가득 들어 있어요.
examples.en: The steamed bun is full of red bean paste.
My mother steamed buns for us herself.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 찐빵 하나에 우유 한 잔 주세요.
examples.en: One warm steamed bun and a glass of milk, please.

examples.ko: 찐빵이 식으면 딱딱해져서 다시 쪄야 해요.
examples.en: When steamed buns cool they get hard, so you have to steam them again.

examples.ko: 편의점에서 파는 호빵과 찐빵은 뭐가 달라요?
examples.en: What's the difference between the steamed buns sold at convenience stores (hobbang) and jjinppang?

explain: 밀가루 반죽에 보통 팥소를 넣고 찜기에 쪄서 만든 빵이에요. 오븐에 굽는 빵과 달리 촉촉하고 쫀득해서 겨울 간식 느낌이 강해요. '호빵'이라고도 많이 불러요.

phrases.en: I bought a red bean steamed bun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 속재료인 팥을 앞에 붙인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common filling, red bean, placed before the name.

phrases.nuance_ko: 갓 쪄서 따뜻한 찐빵을 살 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when buying a freshly steamed, warm bun.

phrases.en: I warmed up a steamed bun from the convenience store and ate it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찐빵을 부르는 다른 이름으로, 특히 겨울에 편의점에서 파는 것을 떠올려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another name for a steamed bun, which people associate with ones sold at convenience stores in winter.

explain_en: It is a steamed bun, usually filled with sweet red bean paste, made from wheat dough steamed in a steamer. Unlike baked bread it is moist and soft-chewy, and it feels like a typical winter snack. People also call it '호빵'.
